headline: Xbox CEO: We have one year to start growing again
summary: Asha Sharma has set a deadline for Xbox to return to player and revenue growth by the end of fiscal year 2027, aiming to improve profits and expand its reach.
details: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has informed staff that the company has until the end of fiscal year 2027, which concludes next June, to achieve growth in both players and revenue. This directive follows significant restructuring and studio layoffs, signaling a critical period for the gaming giant.

Sharma aims to improve Xbox's profits to align with industry averages, emphasizing that "every function and studio will own part of that outcome." This push for profitability is coupled with an ambitious goal to make Xbox "one of the few companies that entertains more than a billion people each day."

The company is focusing on four key priorities for FY27: returning to growth, turning strategic bets into revenue acceleration in FY28-29, and scaling successful initiatives to achieve double-digit growth in players and engagement by FY30.

Xbox currently engages over 100 million people daily, 500 million monthly, and nearly one billion annually. Sharma highlighted that while consoles remain the "flagship experience" and the primary revenue driver, the Xbox OS, Game Pass, Windows, and streaming services are crucial for attracting new players and developers.

The studio system is shifting from a decentralized model to one centered around its strongest franchises and innovative ideas. Xbox plans to develop long-term strategies for its major franchises across various media, including film, television, and consumer products, and is actively seeking new global partnerships.

To capture a larger share of the casual gaming market, Xbox will leverage King, the maker of Candy Crush, and Microsoft Casual Games. Significant new investments are also planned for Minecraft, underscoring its importance to Xbox's future growth strategy.
